title: I Built a Souls-Like Boss Fight in 72 Hours Using AI + Unreal Engine 5
author: Delicious-Shower8401
selftext:
In 3 days I built a complete **playable Souls-like** arena with a player character, boss, environment, animations, cloth physics, combat and lighting.

My workflow was roughly:

* **Prompting + image ideation** — generate prompts and supporting images in 3DAIStudio to speed up concept exploration.
* **3D generation:** create characters, armor, props and environment pieces with Tripo P2.
* **Optimization:** decimate / retopologize the generated meshes, clean topology in Blender and bake the high-poly detail down to lighter meshes.
* **Textures:** generate and modify additional tileable materials, alphas and clothing textures with AI, then manually adjust everything where needed.
* **World building:** build the arena modularly in Blender instead of generating one giant environment mesh. Arrays, curves and reusable pieces made iteration much faster.
* **Characters:** assemble generated parts manually, sculpt problematic areas, rig the characters and fix skin weights.
* **UE5:** set up materials, weapons, animations, collisions, cloth physics, lighting, fog and the actual boss encounter.
* **Coding / setup:** AI coding tools helped with repetitive Unreal tasks and logic, while the actual design decisions, debugging and integration were still done manually.

One thing that became very obvious during this project is that **AI is much more useful as a production accelerator than as a replacement for the workflow itself**.

Tripo AI didn't magically give me a finished game-ready character. What it did was remove a huge chunk of the slow initial modeling work. Instead of starting from an empty Blender scene, I could immediately start making decisions about topology, proportions, materials, rigging and how the asset actually fits into the game.

For ideation and asset prep, I used 3DAIStudio, which helped a lot for generating prompts, reference images, and quickly iterating on visual directions. Its **node-based workflow** made things much faster, and having access to multiple major **3D generators in one place** was genuinely useful during production.

And when you repeat that across dozens of assets, the time savings become pretty ridiculous.

There's still a lot of manual 3D work here: assembling, sculpting, retopo, baking, UVs, rigging, weight painting, optimization, level design, shaders, physics and Unreal setup.
